answers.text: Three lines, same order — drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted. If nothing's noted, I'd still write 'none' rather than skip the line.
List each call by time, customer, topic and outcome.
The finish time doesn't add up — six hours from an 8am start shouldn't spill into the next day. Worth checking.
96 to 118 is more than a 20% rise. And I'd double-check the on-time rate too.
Output 2, it shows the numbers behind the 88%. Output 1 gives you nothing to check.
Email 2 — real numbers, 1,200 to 1,650. Email 1 doesn't say what it's comparing to, so there's nothing to verify.

1. No — that's someone's home address. 2. Yes, it's just a total, no vendor detail. 3. No — the budget isn't signed off yet. 4. Yes, it's already published on their site, so no harm there. 5. No — same reason as the address, that's personal.
I'd redact the hourly rates, and I'd be careful with the non-disclosure clause since it names both parties.
Before the summary goes out, I'd cross-check the stock counts against the system.
Step 1 matters because a bad read carries through, but step 4 — automatic submission — is where I'd put the gate, and it should check that the match is genuinely within tolerance, not just close.
